data.name: Kirtikumar
data.gender_notes: Kirtikumar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Kirti refers to fame and glory, and Kumar refers to a young boy. The name Kirtikumar can be interpreted as 'the mark of the Sun God on a young boy'. In Hindu mythology, the Sun God is revered as a symbol of power, energy, and creativity. This name is believed to bestow upon the child these divine qualities. The name Kirtikumar carries the meaning “Sun God's Mark” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kirtikumar usually hope their child will grow to embody sun god's mark and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Kirtikumar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sun God's Mark.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kirtikumar total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kirtikumar has deep cultural significance in Hindu society. It is derived from the names of the Sun God and the young boy Krishna. The Sun God and Krishna are considered two of the most revered deities in Hinduism. The name Kirtikumar pays homage to their divine power, creativity, and charm. It is believed that naming a child as Kirtikumar will bring him good fortune, blessings, and a victorious spirit.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Kirtikumar also holds great spiritual significance. It signifies the mark of the Divine Child Krishna or the Sun God on a young boy. It is believed that this name brings the divine blessings of these deities upon the child, instilling in him the qualities of power, energy, creativity, and happiness. The child is believed to be a vessel of these deities and is encouraged to live a righteous life filled with love, joy, and devotion.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Kirtikumar is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Kirti' meaning fame and 'Kumar' meaning young boy or prince. This name symbolizes the pursuit of fame and glory, becoming renowned and respected in society through virtuous actions and noble deeds, embodying the spirit of a young, ambitious, and honorable warrior.

vedic_reference.note: Kirtikumar is a name of Indra, the god of rain and thunder in Hindu mythology. He is also associated with the constellation Akshra Kriti.

historical_references.reference: The Hindu calendar refers to the month of Kartik as the month of Lord Kartikeya, also known as Skanda or Kirtikasur. This month is associated with the worship of Lord Kartikeya and is celebrated with great fervour in many parts of India.

Another reference to Kirtikumar can be found in the Puranic literature where Kartikeya is described as the elder son of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati. His name Kartikeya is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Kart' meaning 'to move' and 'Keya' meaning 'son'. He is also known as Skanda or Subrahmanya and is considered the god of war and the leader of the army of the gods.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Kirtikumar continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
